}

.dark #mail.havemail,

 width: 18px;
 height: 12px;
}

First… not a hash tag. Let’s cover some CSS basics briefly:

  • # denotes an ID. This is a unique identifier (only one element in the page should have this ID). #mail refers to the element with the ID “mail”.

  • . denotes a class. This is a non-unique identifier (multiple elements can have the same class). .havemail refers to any element with the class “havemail”.

  • You can join multiple selectors, including elements, IDs, and classes. #mail.havemail refers to the element with the ID “mail” and the class “havemail`. Note that there is no space between them.

  • You can also combine multiple selectors with a space (or some other special characters). This defines a relationship between the two selectors. .dark #mail.havemail refers to the element with the ID “mail” and the class “havemail”, that is a descendent of any element with the class “dark”.

You can read more about Selectors and other CSS topics.

If you don’t care for any of that, basically just add .dark with a space before any of the existing selectors. .arrow-upvote becomes .dark .arrow-upvote, and .expando-button.selftext.collapsed:hover becomes .dark .expando-button.selftext.collapsed:hover.
